answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a rising identity bond: each new agent identity must lock a stake that grows with how many identities one operator already controls. Honest agents earn fees and reclaim their bond; a caught double-voter forfeits it. The attacker's cost climbs in a spiral because every extra fake identity needs a larger deposit than the last. An ivory ledger records every bond, and collateral in juniper is burned on fraud, so buying enough fake identities to sway a vote costs far more than any dishonest gain.
